page: Amazon Web Services c8g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation that eliminates simultaneous multithreading contention. Hardware cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. The instance is allocated 64 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, supported by baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. There is no bundled local NVMe storage and no auxiliary GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and high memory throughput. The system reaches a top-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 21249.0 alongside top-tier large-block memory read bandwidth of 391.61 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 171.76 GB/sec. PassMark database operations also place in the top tier at 46834.4 operations, while Redis SET performance registers 67.77 million operations per second. In single-core compute tasks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core testing, the processor performs in the middle 50 percent bracket. Static web serving throughput reaches 72.97 GB/sec, reflecting efficient packet handling and caching subsystem architecture.

The 1:1 execution model delivers predictable processing capacity without the latency jitter often introduced by hyperthreaded x86 designs. While single-thread instruction throughput remains moderate, the Graviton microarchitecture delivers favorable compute density and memory transfer rates per resource unit. Tradeoffs include the total absence of onboard ephemeral NVMe drives, necessitating network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent file access, and lower inference speeds on large 70B language models due to memory constraints and lack of specialized matrix extensions. The c8g.8xlarge is suited for scalable microservices, Clang-based compilation pipelines, high-concurrency web tiers, and batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 architecture. It delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores at 2.8 GHz, paired with 64 GB of system memory, 36 MB of L3 cache, and a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-core performance, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 21249.0 and large-block memory read throughput of 391.61 GB/sec. The instance excels at multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and software compilation, while single-core compute performance remains average. Because each vCPU corresponds to an independent execution core, the architecture prevents hyperthreading contention and maximizes compute throughput per resource allocation. The c8g.8xlarge is well matched for Clang build clusters, distributed web services, containerized microservices, and high-throughput Redis caching layers requiring consistent processing and fast memory access.
